context.title: Jonathan's Arrows
context.summary: David and Jonathan agree on a test: if Saul is angry when David misses the new moon feast, Jonathan will warn him with a signal of arrows. Saul explodes in rage and even throws his spear at Jonathan. The friends say a tearful farewell.
context.background: The new moon began each month with sacrifices and a festive meal (Numbers 10:10). Saul tells Jonathan he will never be king while David lives (v. 31). Jonathan asks David to show kindness to his family forever (vv. 14–15), a promise David later keeps to Jonathan's son Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9).

customs.note: In the KJV, 'artillery' simply means weapons, here Jonathan's bow and arrows.

watchFor: Jonathan's covenant reaches to 'the house of David' (vv. 14–17).
Saul's anger turns on his own son (vv. 30–33).
'The Lord be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever' (v. 42).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Jonathan
people.summary: The eldest son of king Saul, and the bosom friend of David. He is first mentioned when he was about thirty years of age, some time after his father’s accession to the throne (1 Sam. 13:2).

people.name: Saul
people.summary: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation. The singular providential circumstances connected with his election as king are recorded in 1 Sam. 8-10.

people.name: Abner
people.summary: Father of light; i.e., “enlightening”, the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul’s army (1 Sam. 14:50; 17:55; 20:25).

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

places.name: Naioth
places.summary: Dwellings, the name given to the prophetical college established by Samuel near Ramah. It consisted of a cluster of separate dwellings, and hence its name.

places.name: Ramah
places.summary: The same as Ramathaim-zophim, a town of Mount Ephraim (1 Sam. 1:1, 19).

places.name: Bethlehem
places.summary: A city in the “hill country” of Judah. It was originally called Ephrath (Gen. 35:16, 19; 48:7; Ruth 4:11). It was also called Beth-lehem Ephratah (Micah 5:2), Beth-lehem-judah (1 Sam. 17:12), and “the city of David” (Luke 2:4).

events.title: Reign of Saul
events.summary: Passage: 1 Samuel 10:1–31:2. People: Saul. Lasted about 40 years.
